svg.title: Four kinds of edge in the event DAG
svg.desc: Animated: one small event DAG with every edge classified by why it exists: required by the domain, required only by a path chosen early, a resource order whose direction was chosen greedily, or conservative. Today every kind reaches CHUGG as a hard precedence constraint.
svg.metadata: ["Two jobs. Job A retrieves the car on T17 into bay B21, which still holds empty tray T21; tray assignment also moves T15, which stands on T17's chosen route. Job B, a clean, moves two trays off waypoints. Seven events after AGV assignment (AGV-1 serves job A's moves, AGV-2 the blocker and job B's first move, AGV-3 its second); AGV approach and lift events are left out.", "Causal edges (green): an effect of one event is a precondition of the next. Until B21 is in retrieve mode its overdrive-plate area blocks the aisle, the bay node must be empty before T17 enters, and the car must be in the bay before the hand-over. Every valid plan contains these orders.", "Path-dependent edge (blue): T15 must leave P15 only because T17's route was fixed through P15 before motion planning. With another route, or with T15 leaving in time, the edge is not needed. These come from occupancy checks (freeing_moves) and path repairs.", "Resource-order edge (amber): AGV-2 does the blocker move and job B's first move, so one must come first, but either order is valid. The direction was fixed by request order and assignment: in scheduling terms, a disjunctive constraint whose choice was made greedily.", "Conservative edge (red): rule B makes each new event of a job wait for all of the job's current leaves, so job B's two moves are chained although they use different AGVs, trays and places.", "What the motion planner receives today: all seven edges as hard precedence. A solver that knew the kinds could keep green, choose amber, let paths decide blue and drop red, and so find plans with more parallelism."]

g.text: Four kinds of edge in the event DAG

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The event DAG is a partial-order plan. Its edges record different things, but the pipeline fixes all of them before timing and geometry are known. Example and classification are illustrative.
